title: SLO-driven regional fanout and graceful degradation for downstream dependencies
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Implement an SLO-driven resilience layer that automatically performs regional failover, adaptive circuit breaking, and graded load shedding for key downstream dependencies (Redis, Kafka, Postgres) with minimal user-visible regressions. Motivation: recent incidents showed single-dependency overloads cause cascading latency spikes. Rather than one-size-fits-all connpool throttles, we want a coordinated strategy across SDK/gateway/runtime that enforces tail-SLOs with prioritized degradation for noncritical features.
acceptance_criteria: Platform maintains 99.9% availability of core API routes under a simulated 3x downstream latency spike for 15 minutes by applying degradation rules
P99 token-gen latency remains below 350ms when Redis is operating at 50% error rate by falling back to local cache and async write-behind
Circuit breakers for each dependency transition correctly (closed->open->half-open) based on rolling-window latency+error thresholds and expose metrics (state, open_duration, failures) to console
Connection pools per-region and per-priority enforce caps; observed rejected-by-pool rate matches configured thresholds and returns 429 with Retry-After to SDK callers
End-to-end chaos test simulating region outage within 60s fails over to secondary region for read operations and returns graceful degraded responses for write-heavy paths as configured
proposed_solution_steps: Instrument per-dependency SLOs: define latency and error SLOs for Redis/Kafka/Postgres that map to feature-level criticality
Implement SLO Controller in edge/runtime that computes per-dependency 'pressure' scores (0..100) from rolling 1m/5m windows of p50/p95/p99 latency and error-rate

Adaptive policy engine: map pressure score to actions: (0-30 no action),(31-60 shed noncritical read/get requests),(61-80 route to regional fallback/local cache or disk buffer),(81-100 open circuit and reject with graceful partial responses)

Circuit breaker semantics: multi-signal (err rate, tail latency, connection exhaustion). Use token-bucket for reopening: allow probes at controlled RPS, restore to closed only on sustained healthy probes

Connection pooling changes: introduce priority-aware pools (high/normal/low) per dependency and per region. Pools expose soft_limit and hard_limit. Soft_limit triggers shed of low-priority requests, hard_limit rejects with 429

Multi-region failover: implement fanout fallback: primary->hedge to secondary region for reads when p95 exceeds threshold. Maintain sticky session keys for affinity for low-latency paths; enable async cross-region replication for eventual consistency where applicable

Degradation strategies by dependency: Redis: local LRU cache + stale-while-revalidate + async write-behind; Kafka: switch to durable local disk buffer + backpressure to producers + delayed publish; Postgres: route reads to replicas, turn writes into async queue with immediate partial acknowledgement for best-effort non-critical workflows
Telemetry: add metrics for pressure_score, pool_utilization, circuit_state, shed_count_by_feature, fallback_rate_by_region, queued_writes_count
Runbook and SLA mapping: update runbooks to include thresholds that trigger on-call paging and automated mitigation playbooks
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Prioritization model: prefer feature-level criticality mapping (auth/billing/identity = highest) over blanket per-tenant priorities to reduce blast radius
Stale responses: adopt stale-while-revalidate for cache fallbacks to preserve latency SLOs at the cost of eventual consistency for low-priority features
Async write-behind: improves availability for writes but increases risk window; we add strong auditing and backfill job to reconcile failures
Hedging reads to secondary region increases cross-region egress and cost; hedging limited by configurable rate and only triggered when SLO pressure_score exceeds threshold
Separate pools by priority adds complexity but prevents low-priority tasks from starving high-priority traffic under connection exhaustion
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Double-writes or out-of-order writes during failover. Mitigation: idempotency keys and sequence numbers for write-behind queues
Risk: Increased egress costs due to hedging. Mitigation: configurable cap and metrics to surface cost tradeoffs to product owners
Risk: Operator confusion from more moving parts (pressure scores, pools). Mitigation: dashboard + single-pane-of-glass view and clear runbook playbooks
Risk: Accidental data loss when draining to local disk buffer. Mitigation: persist with fsync semantics and retention policy; automatic replay job; alert on buffer saturation
testing_plan: Unit tests for SLO controller logic and mapping rules
Integration test harness that simulates Redis/Kafka/Postgres latency and error patterns and validates expected degradation actions
Load test: run chaos scenario with 3x latency and 30% errors in primary region for 15 minutes; assert API SLOs and measured shed rates
Chaos experiments: region failover, partitioned cluster, slow disk for Kafka buffers
Canary rollout: 1% traffic -> 10% -> 50% with automated rollback if platform-level metrics breach thresholds
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): implement pressure_score telemetry and basic pool changes behind feature flag on staging
Phase 2 (internal canary): enable adaptive policies for noncritical features in production for 5% of accounts; monitor
Phase 3: expand to 50% accounts and enable hedging for read-heavy endpoints; validate cost and SLOs
Phase 4: full rollout and enable write-behind for designated noncritical write paths; update runbooks
Rollback criteria: spike in error-rate for critical routes, p99 increase >20% vs baseline, or data replay failure rate >0.1%
observability_requirements: Expose pressure_score and mapping reason in request traces
Dashboards: per-dependency heatmap, pool utilization, open-breaker counts, fallback rates by region
Alerting: sustained pressure_score > 70 for 2m triggers paging; buffer saturation > 80% triggers high-severity alert
Sampling: ensure samples include traces where fallback or shedding occurred for downstream debugging
runbook_snippets: If p95 Redis latency > 200ms and pressure_score>60: enable read-hedging to secondary region for 2m and increase cache TTL to 60s for noncritical keys
If Redis circuit breaker opens: confirm local cache fill rate; if buffer >50% notify infra and follow replay job to drain writes
If Postgres replicas lag > 5s during failover: switch critical writes to limited mode (reject noncritical writes with 429) and page DB on-call
If Kafka local buffer exceeds 90%: pause low-priority producers and run drain job; if draining fails after 10m, degrade analytics pipeline
